name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
description: A common fungal disease of tomato causing circular leaf spots with dark borders and light centers. It spreads rapidly in warm, wet weather and can cause extensive defoliation, reducing fruit yield and quality.
symptoms: Small circular spots with dark brown edges and gray centers
Tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) visible in lesion centers
Spots appearing first on lower leaves and progressing upward
Leaves turning yellow and dropping prematurely
causes: Extended leaf wetness from rain or overhead irrigation
Fungal survival on crop debris and solanaceous weeds
Rain splash dispersing spores to healthy leaves
treatments: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb at first spots
Spray copper-based fungicides for organic production
Remove infected lower leaves to reduce inoculum
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
Space plants adequately for good air circulation
Use drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet
